1. Dataset Overview

The dataset lists current-price GSDP figures (in ₹ crore) for 34 states and union territories across 11 financial years (2011-12 to 2021-22), along with year-on-year % growth columns. Out of 374 GSDP data points, 44 are missing (~11.8%).

⚠ Data completeness note

The most recent year, 2021-22, is missing for 15 entities — including major economies like Maharashtra, Gujarat, West Bengal and Bihar — most likely because these figures had not yet been reported at the time of data collection. Using 2021-22 as a "current" snapshot would therefore wrongly rank these states as small or absent. To keep rankings and comparisons accurate, this report uses 2020-21 (the most recent year with data for all but 2 minor entities) as the reference "current" year for all cross-state comparisons, while trend charts still show all 11 years including the partial 2021-22.

Jammu & Kashmir also appears twice — as the erstwhile state (pre-2019) and the newly formed union territory (2019-20 onward) after bifurcation — reflecting a genuine structural break in the data, not a data-quality issue.

2. Year-wise Total GDP (National Trend)

Sum of GSDP across all reporting states/UTs for each year.

  • National aggregate GSDP grew from ₹86.3 lakh crore (2011-12) to a peak of ₹210.5 lakh crore (2020-21) — roughly a 2.4x increase over the decade.
  • The visible drop in 2021-22 is a reporting-gap artifact (see Section 1), not a real economic contraction.
  • Growth was steady year-on-year with no visible decline until the COVID-affected slowdown in 2020-21's growth rate (though the level itself still rose slightly, since some states grew even as others contracted).

3. High & Low GDP States, Top 10 (2020-21)

  • Highest GSDP: Maharashtra (₹27.1 lakh crore), followed by Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.
  • Lowest GSDP (among states): Mizoram (₹29,214 crore) — smallest economy among the north-eastern states.
  • The top 5 states (Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat) together account for a disproportionately large share of national output, highlighting significant regional concentration.

4. GDP Trend Over Time — Leading States

  • Maharashtra has consistently led in absolute GSDP throughout the entire 11-year window.
  • Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh show the steepest upward trajectories among the top states, gradually closing the gap with Gujarat.
  • All top states show a visible flattening in growth momentum around 2020-21, consistent with the pandemic-driven slowdown.

5. State-wise Growth Rate — Fastest & Slowest (11-yr CAGR)

Compound Annual Growth Rate computed from each state's first to last available data point.

  • Fastest-growing: Mizoram (16.7% CAGR), Madhya Pradesh (14.0%), Tripura (13.6%), Karnataka (13.0%), Sikkim (12.9%) — a mix of smaller north-eastern states catching up from a low base, and larger states like MP and Karnataka industrializing rapidly.
  • Slowest-growing: Meghalaya (6.5%), Goa (7.3%), Uttarakhand (7.8%), Punjab (8.4%), Jharkhand (8.6%) — Goa's low CAGR partly reflects a sharp GSDP contraction in 2012-13 and 2013-14 (mining-sector downturn) from which it took years to recover.

6. GDP Distribution & Outlier Detection (2020-21)

  • The distribution is strongly right-skewed — most states cluster below ₹10 lakh crore, while a handful of large economies pull the tail far to the right.
  • Using the IQR method, Maharashtra is flagged as a statistical outlier — its GSDP is so much larger than the median state that it sits well beyond the upper whisker.
  • This confirms the concentration seen in Section 3: India's state economy sizes are highly unequal, not normally distributed.

7. Correlation Between Years

Correlation of GSDP levels across states, year to year — measures how consistently states retain their relative ranking over time.

  • Correlation between consecutive and even distant years is consistently above 0.95, showing that relative state rankings are very stable — large economies stay large, small economies stay small.
  • Correlation is marginally weaker between years furthest apart (e.g. 2011-12 vs 2021-22), reflecting gradual re-ranking as faster-growing states close the gap.

8. Contribution of Each State to National GDP (2020-21)

  • The top 10 states together contribute the large majority of national GSDP, with the remaining ~24 states/UTs collectively making up the "Others" slice.
  • Maharashtra alone contributes well over 10% of total measured GSDP — more than double most other large states.

9. State Ranking — Regional Standing (2020-21)

States grouped into South, West, North, Central, East, Northeast, and Island regions.

  • South is the largest regional bloc by GSDP (led by Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana), followed by West (Maharashtra + Gujarat) and North.
  • Northeast and Island regions remain far smaller in absolute terms, consistent with their lower population and industrial base.

10. Increment Over the Decade (2011-12 → 2020-21)

  • Mizoram grew over 300% in GSDP terms over the decade — the highest percentage increase of any state, off a small base.
  • Madhya Pradesh, Tripura, Sikkim and Karnataka also more than tripled/doubled their GSDP, reflecting broad-based expansion beyond just the traditionally large economies.

11. GDP Growth Rate Heatmap (State × Year)

  • The heatmap makes the 2020-21 column stand out as a broad band of red/negative or near-zero growth across almost every state — the clearest visual signature of COVID-19's economic impact.
  • 2021-22 (where reported) is uniformly bright green, showing strong across-the-board recovery.
  • A few negative-growth cells also appear in earlier years for individual states (e.g. Goa in 2012-13/2013-14), pointing to state-specific downturns unrelated to COVID.

12. GDP Growth Rate After COVID-19

  • Average state growth rate fell from ~10.6% (2018-19) and ~9.5% (2019-20) to just ~2.7% in 2020-21 — the pandemic year.
  • Recovery was sharp: average growth rebounded to ~15.1% in 2021-22 (among states that reported), exceeding pre-pandemic levels — consistent with a low-base effect plus genuine rebound demand.
  • Hardest hit in 2020-21: Uttarakhand (-3.9%), Meghalaya (-3.7%), Kerala (-3.0%), Himachal Pradesh (-1.6%), Jharkhand (-1.3%) — a mix of tourism-dependent (Uttarakhand, HP, Kerala) and mining/industry-dependent (Jharkhand) economies.
